coptic_restorations.basis: Single-letter completion of ϣⲓ 'measure' yielding the idiom ⲉⲙⲛ̄ ϣⲓ ⲁⲣⲁϥ 'there is no measure to it' — the breath-offspring is so continuous and pervasive (issuing from all the members) that it cannot be measured. Editor's reading is grammatically and lexically secure.

Greek loanword ἐπιθυμία broken across line-break: ⲉⲡⲓⲑ̄ⲩ- + ⲙⲓⲁ continuing in the next line. Single missing vowel ⲩ. The phrase ⲧϩⲏⲇⲟⲛⲏ ⲛⲧⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ 'pleasure of desire' is a stock formula for sexual generation, here producing the fourth offspring (inner conjunction of love and wisdom).

Completion of ⲡⲉϥⲙⲉⲩⲉ 'his thought' (second of the five faculties per the lexicon — ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ). Triplet ⲡⲉϥⲟⲩⲱϣⲉ ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ — ⲡⲉϥⲙⲉⲩⲉ — ⲧⲉϥⲁⲅⲁⲡⲏ ('desire of heart — thought — love') describes the parents' affective stance toward the begotten fifth offspring.

ⲧϥ-ⲁⲅ-ⲁⲡⲏ = ⲧⲉϥⲁⲅⲁⲡⲏ 'his love' (Greek ἀγάπη); the visible -ⲁⲡⲏ requires preceding ⲁⲅ to form the loanword. Closes the standard triad desire–thought–love by which parents recognize the bodily offspring (ⲡⲓⲝⲡⲟ ⲛ̄ⲥⲱⲙⲁⲧⲓⲕⲟⲛ).

english_restorations.basis: ϣⲓ = 'measure'; the breath-offspring issues continually from every member and cannot be reckoned.
ⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ = ἐπιθυμία 'desire'; the standard pairing with ἡδονή 'pleasure' for procreative joining renders 'pleasure of desire'.
ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ = 'thought' per the corpus lexicon (the second of the five faculties); fits the desire-thought-love triad.
ⲧⲁⲅⲁⲡⲏ = 'love' (ἀγάπη) per the lexicon; closes the parents' affective triad toward their begotten bodily offspring.

restoration_note: All four gaps are short scribal lacunae within fixed lexical items: ϣⲓ 'measure' completes the immeasurability of the breath-offspring; ⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ is a loanword broken across a line; ⲡⲉϥⲙⲉⲩⲉ 'his thought' and ⲧⲉϥⲁⲅⲁⲡⲏ 'his love' close the standard desire–thought–love triad by which the parents acknowledge the fifth, bodily offspring while ignoring the four hidden ones (breath, speech, operation-under-shame, inner conjunction). All restorations are constrained by partial traces, surrounding morphology, and the corpus lexicon.
